title: The Mordell conjecture after Lawrence and Venkatesh
summary: Faltings's theorem, that a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus at least two over a number field has only finitely many rational points, proved by the method of Lawrence and Venkatesh. The fibres of an auxiliary abelian-by-finite family over the curve carry global p-adic Galois representations of bounded dimension, restricted ramification and fixed weight, of which Faltings's finiteness lemma leaves only finitely many. Through the crystalline comparison theorem these representations are read off from a p-adic period map on residue disks, which agrees as a power series with the complex period map. Big monodromy of the Kodaira–Parshin family, computed with Dehn twists in mapping class groups, makes the period map Zariski dense; a bound on the centraliser of the semilinear Frobenius, obtained by enlarging the residue fields through an Aff(q)-covering, and a purity argument that controls the failure of semisimplicity then confine the rational points of each residue disk to the zero set of a nonzero analytic function. The S-unit theorem is the first worked instance of the method.
readme:
# The Mordell conjecture after Lawrence and Venkatesh

## Purpose

This roadmap proves **Faltings's theorem**: if $K$ is a number field and $Y/K$ is a smooth projective
geometrically connected curve of genus $g \ge 2$, then $Y(K)$ is finite. The proof follows Brian Lawrence
and Akshay Venkatesh, *Diophantine problems and $p$-adic period mappings* (Invent. Math. 221 (2020),
893–999; arXiv:1807.02721v3), §§2–8. It is an alternative to Faltings's height-theoretic proof and does not
use heights, the Tate conjecture or the Shafarevich conjecture for abelian varieties. Along the way it proves
the **S-unit theorem** (LV Theorem 4.1) by the same method.

## Scope

In scope: the paper's §2 (linear algebra, Faltings's finiteness lemma, friendly places and the purity
lemmas 2.8–2.10, the group $\mathrm{Aff}(q)$, symplectic Goursat and transvection lemmas), §3 in the
generality of polarized abelian schemes over a finite étale cover of the base (Gauss–Manin transport on
residue disks, complex and $p$-adic period maps, Lemmas 3.1–3.3, Proposition 3.4), §4 (the S-unit
equation), §§5–6 (abelian-by-finite families, $\mathrm{size}_v$, Proposition 5.3 and Lemmas 6.1–6.4),
§7 (the Hurwitz construction and the Kodaira–Parshin family), §8 (mapping class groups, $\mathrm{Aff}(q)$-covers
and the monodromy theorem 8.1) and Theorem 5.4. The surface topology that §8 and the monodromy of the Legendre
family in §4 rest on (mapping class groups, Dehn twists, the Birman exact sequence, families of branched covers)
is carried by layer LV.5, because no atlas roadmap owns it; the restructure proposal of the blueprint packet
assigns it to a new roadmap.

Not in scope: LV §§9–12 (hypersurfaces, the Bakker–Tsimerman theorem, reductive-group combinatorics, point
counting), and Lemmas 2.2, 2.4–2.6, which only those sections use. The general machinery the proof consumes
(period rings and period functors, crystalline cohomology, the crystalline comparison theorem, abelian schemes
and their degree-one realizations, étale fundamental groups, class field theory, Chebotarev, algebraic groups,
singular homology, covering spaces) is owned by the roadmaps named in each layer.

## Conventions

- $K \subset \bar{\mathbb Q}$ is a number field; $G_K = \mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb Q}/K)$. For a finite place
  $\wp$ of $K$, $q_\wp$ is the size of its residue field and $\mathrm{Frob}_\wp$ is the **arithmetic**
  Frobenius (Mathlib `IsArithFrobAt`); $\mathrm{Frob}_\wp^{\mathrm{geom}} = \mathrm{Frob}_\wp^{-1}$.
- A continuous representation $\rho : G_K \to \mathrm{GL}(V)$ on a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q_p$-vector
  space is **pure of weight $w$ outside a finite set $T$** if for every finite place $\wp \notin T$ it is
  unramified at $\wp$ and every root of the characteristic polynomial of $\rho(\mathrm{Frob}_\wp^{\mathrm{geom}})$
  is an algebraic number all of whose complex absolute values equal $q_\wp^{w/2}$; it has **integral
  Frobenius polynomials outside $T$** if these characteristic polynomials lie in $\mathbb Z[X]$. With this
  normalization $H^w_{\mathrm{et}}(X_{\bar K},\mathbb Q_p)$ of a smooth projective variety with good reduction
  outside $T$ is pure of weight $w$ and $\mathbb Q_p(1)$ has weight $-2$. LV state their Lemma 2.3 with
  "unramified outside $S$" while applying it to representations ramified above $p$; here $T$ always contains
  the places above $p$.
- Local class field theory: $\mathrm{Art}_{K_v}$ sends uniformizers to arithmetic Frobenius and satisfies
  $\chi_{\mathrm{cyc}}(\mathrm{Art}_{K_v}(u)) = N_{K_v/\mathbb Q_p}(u)^{-1}$ for $u \in \mathcal O_{K_v}^\times$
  (Tau Ceti `ClassFieldTheory`, Layer 7).
- $p$-adic Hodge theory is covariant: $D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V) = (V \otimes_{\mathbb Q_p} B_{\mathrm{cris}})^{G_{K_v}}$,
  $D_{\mathrm{dR}}(V) = (V \otimes B_{\mathrm{dR}})^{G_{K_v}}$. Filtrations are recorded by their **jumps**:
  $D_{\mathrm{dR}}(\mathbb Q_p(n))$ has its jump in degree $-n$ (Brinon–Conrad, Example 6.3.1), so a jump $j$
  is the Hodge–Tate weight $-j$ in the `PadicHodgeTheory` convention $\mathrm{HT}(\chi_p)=+1$. For an abelian
  variety with good reduction, $D_{\mathrm{cris}}(H^1_{\mathrm{et}})$ is $H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}$ with its Hodge
  filtration, jumps $0$ and $1$.
- The **weight of a filtration** $F^\bullet$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional vector space $V$ with $F^0V=V$ is
  $\mathrm{weight}_F(V) = \sum_{j} j \dim \mathrm{gr}^j V / \dim V$ (LV (2.2)), i.e. $t_H(V)/\dim V$ in
  Brinon–Conrad's notation.
- For $K_v/\mathbb Q_p$ unramified of degree $f_v$, $\sigma$ is the arithmetic Frobenius of $K_v$; a
  crystalline Frobenius $\varphi$ is $\sigma$-semilinear and $\varphi^{f_v}$ is $K_v$-linear.
- A **curve** over a scheme $S$ is a smooth proper morphism of relative dimension one with geometrically
  connected fibres. Grassmannians parametrize **subspaces**. $\mathrm{LGr}(V,\omega)$ is the variety of
  Lagrangian subspaces of a $2d$-dimensional symplectic space; it has dimension $d(d+1)/2$.
- Symplectic transvections are $T_v^r(x) = x + r\langle v,x\rangle v$ (LV (2.4)); for a Dehn twist,
  Farb–Margalit's $\Psi(T_b)([a]) = [a] + \hat\imath(a,b)[b]$ fixes $\langle v, x\rangle = \hat\imath(x, v)$.
- $\mathrm{Aff}(q) = \{x \mapsto ax+b\} \subset \mathrm{Sym}(\mathbb F_q)$ for a prime $q \ge 3$;
  $H_q = \mathbb F_q^\times$ is the stabilizer of $0$.
- $\mathrm{size}_v(E)$ is the proportion of elements of a finite $G_K$-set $E$ unramified at $v$ that lie in
  $\mathrm{Frob}_v$-orbits of size $< 8$ (LV Definition 5.2).

## Sources

Lawrence–Venkatesh (arXiv:1807.02721v3) is the primary source; Brinon–Conrad's CMI notes for $p$-adic Hodge
theory; Farb–Margalit, *A primer on mapping class groups* (v5.0) for §8; Milne, *Complex Multiplication*, for
CM fields and infinity types; Faltings (1983) and Deligne (Sém. Bourbaki 616) for the finiteness lemma;
Berthelot–Ogus for crystalline cohomology; SGA 1 for fundamental groups and Riemann existence; K. Conrad,
*Strassmann's theorem and an application*, for zeros of $p$-adic power series.

## Layers

| Layer | Content | Paper |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LV.0 | semilinear centralizers, $\mathrm{Aff}(q)$, counting lemmas, symplectic transvections and Goursat | §2.1, §2.6, §2.7, §5 |
| LV.1 | Faltings's finiteness lemma, friendly places, purity of Hodge weights | §§2.3–2.5 |
| LV.2 | abelian-by-finite families, good models, Gauss–Manin transport, crystalline Frobenius on fibres | §§3.1–3.3, Def. 5.1 |
| LV.3 | Lagrangian period varieties, complex and $p$-adic period maps, Lemmas 3.1–3.3, Strassmann | §§3.2–3.4 |
| LV.4 | crystalline comparison for the fibres, Frobenius-centralizer orbits, finiteness criterion, Proposition 3.4 | §3.5, §6 |
| LV.5 | surfaces, mapping class groups, Dehn twists, point pushing, families of branched covers | §8.1 (with Farb–Margalit) |
| LV.6 | the S-unit theorem | §4 |
| LV.7 | $\mathrm{size}_v$, Lemmas 6.1–6.4, Proposition 5.3 | §§5, 6 |
| LV.8 | Hurwitz spaces, reduced Pryms, the Kodaira–Parshin family and the fibre map (5.5) | §7, §5 |
| LV.9 | $\mathrm{Aff}(q)$-covers, primitive homology, lifted monodromy, Lemmas 8.2–8.4, normal form | §§8.2–8.4, 8.6 |
| LV.10 | Lemmas 8.6–8.10, Theorem 8.1, full monodromy of the Kodaira–Parshin family | §§8.2.3, 8.5–8.6 |
| LV.11 | choice of $q$ and $v$, the size bound (5.4), Theorem 5.4 | §5 |

## Non-goals

LV §§9–12 are not part of this roadmap. Faltings's height-theoretic route (`FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems`
R28.5 and `HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions` RP.4) is not used; the Hermite–Minkowski node of
`FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems` R28.1 is the only input taken from that roadmap.

stages.title: Semilinear centralizers, the affine group Aff(q) and symplectic monodromy lemmas
stages.description:
Linear algebra and group theory used throughout the Lawrence–Venkatesh argument (LV §2.1, §2.6, §2.7 and the
counting in the proof of Theorem 5.4).

**Targets.**
- *Centralizer of a semilinear automorphism* (LV Lemma 2.1): for a field automorphism $\sigma$ of $E$ of
  finite order $e$ with fixed field $F$ and a $\sigma$-semilinear bijection $\varphi$ of an $E$-vector space
  $V$, the centralizer $Z(\varphi) \subseteq \mathrm{End}_E(V)$ is an $F$-subalgebra with
  $\dim_F Z(\varphi) = \dim_E Z(\varphi^e) \le (\dim_E V)^2$; the splitting
  $E \otimes_F \Omega \cong \Omega^{\mathrm{Hom}_F(E,\Omega)}$; the unramified form used in LV Lemma 6.2
  ($Z(\varphi)\subseteq Z(\varphi^{f_v})$, a $K_v$-algebra of dimension $\le n^2$ whose unit group is a smooth
  connected $K_v$-group).
- *The affine group* $\mathrm{Aff}(q) \le \mathrm{Sym}(\mathbb F_q)$ for a prime $q\ge3$: order $q(q-1)$,
  $\lambda : \mathrm{Aff}(q) \to \mathbb F_q^\times$ with kernel the translations, trivial centralizer and
  self-normalizing in $\mathrm{Sym}(\mathbb F_q)$, cycle types of its elements; LV Lemma 2.11 on the
  commutator-product map $\mathrm{Aff}(q)^{2s} \to \mathbb F_q$ (image and equal fibres).
- *Counting*: the number of generating $k$-tuples of $\mathbb Z/N$ is
  $N^k\prod_{\ell\mid N}(1-\ell^{-k}) \ge N^k/2$ for $k \ge 2$; a subgroup $B$ of a finite abelian group $A$
  with a perfect $\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$-valued pairing and $\langle B,B\rangle=0$ has $|B|^2 \le |A|$; a
  representation preserving a nondegenerate bilinear form up to scalars has every minimal nonzero
  subrepresentation of dimension at most half (LV (6.8)).
- *Symplectic lemmas*: the symplectic transvection $T_v^r$ with its API; Zariski closures of transvection
  powers; LV Lemma 2.13 and Lemma 2.14 (connected intersection graph); Ribet's Lie-algebra Goursat lemma;
  LV Lemma 2.12 (a Zariski-closed subgroup of $\mathrm{Sp}(V)^N$ surjecting on each factor, with unipotent
  pairs of distinct fixed-space dimension, is everything).

**Inputs.** Zariski closures of abstract subgroups, Lie algebras of closed subgroups, identity components and
the structure of $\mathrm{Sp}(V)$ (connected, centre $\pm1$, almost simple, $\mathfrak{sp}(V)$ simple with inner
automorphisms, generation by transvections) from `ReductiveGroups` Layers 2, 3, 6, 7; unramified extensions of
local fields (`LocalFieldsRamification` Layer 2).

**Acceptance.** $\mathrm{Aff}(3) \cong S_3$; Lemma 2.1 for $E=\mathbb Q_{p^2}$, $F=\mathbb Q_p$ and
$\varphi=\sigma\oplus\sigma$ on $E^2$, where $Z(\varphi)=M_2(\mathbb Q_p)$ and $Z(\varphi^2)=M_2(E)$ both have
dimension $4$; $N = 6$, $k = 2$ gives $24 \ge 18$ generating pairs; for $\mathrm{Aff}(3)$ and $s = 2$ there are
$810$ generating quadruples with nonzero commutator product.

stages.title: Galois representations: Faltings's finiteness lemma, friendly places and purity of Hodge weights
stages.description:
Global Galois-representation inputs (LV §§2.3–2.5).

**Targets.**
- *Faltings's finiteness lemma* (LV Lemma 2.3, with the ramification set $T$ containing the places above $p$):
  for $K$, a finite set $T$ of finite places, integers $w$ and $d$, there are finitely many isomorphism
  classes of semisimple continuous $\rho: G_K \to \mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb Q_p)$ unramified, pure of weight $w$
  and with integral Frobenius polynomials outside $T$; with characteristic-zero Brauer–Nesbitt, the
  Faltings–Deligne finite test set and finiteness of integer Weil polynomials.
- *Friendly places* (LV Definition 2.7): the largest CM-or-totally-real subfield $E_K$ of $K$; a place is
  friendly if it is unramified over $\mathbb Q$ and, when $K$ has a CM subfield, lies over a place of $E_K^+$
  inert in $E_K$.
- *Pure characters at friendly places* (LV Lemma 2.8, stated on units), with local algebraicity of de Rham
  $\mathbb Q_p$-characters, the infinity-type relation from global reciprocity and the factorization through
  $E_K$ (Milne, CM, Proposition 4.9).
- *Hodge weights of pure representations* (LV Lemmas 2.9, 2.10): the weight of the Hodge filtration of
  $D_{\mathrm{dR}}(V|_{G_{K_v}})$ is $w/2$ at a friendly $v$, and
  $\sum_{u\mid v}[L_u:K_v]\,a_u(\rho) = [L:K]\,w/2$ for representations of $G_L$.
- *Fibre representations of abelian varieties*: $H^1_{\mathrm{et}}(A_{\bar L},\mathbb Q_p)$ is pure of weight
  one with integral Frobenius polynomials outside the bad places and the places above $p$, crystalline at good
  places above $p$, with a perfect alternating pairing to $\mathbb Q_p(-1)$.

**Inputs.** Continuous representations (`ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations` R01.1), good-reduction Frobenius
polynomials (R01.6), Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich (`NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties` R11.5), Weil numbers and
Weil's theorem (`DeligneWeightsAndPurity` DWP.0, DWP.1), purity predicates (`WeightsInEtaleCohomology` R34.1),
Chebotarev (`Chebotarev` Layer 10), local and global reciprocity (`ClassFieldTheory` Layers 7, 11),
$D_{\mathrm{dR}}$ (`PadicHodgeTheory` R06.2), crystallinity of good-reduction Tate modules (R06.6), Weil
pairings (`AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli` A3), étale $H^1$ of abelian varieties
(`SchemeAndStackFoundations` SF.3), Hermite–Minkowski (`FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems` R28.1 node).

**Acceptance.** $K=\mathbb Q$: every unramified $p$ is friendly and Lemma 2.8 reads $\eta=\chi_{\mathrm{cyc}}^{-w/2}$
up to finite order on inertia; $\mathbb Q_p(-1)$ has weight $2$ and jump $1$; for an imaginary quadratic $K$,
friendly places lie over primes inert in $K$.

stages.title: Abelian-by-finite families, good models and Gauss–Manin transport on residue disks
stages.description:
The families to which the method is applied, and the identification of the de Rham cohomology of nearby fibres
(LV §§3.1–3.3 and Definition 5.1), for polarized abelian schemes over a finite étale cover of the base.

**Targets.**
- *Abelian-by-finite family* (LV Definition 5.1) $X \xrightarrow{f} Y' \xrightarrow{\pi} Y$ and its *good model*
  over $\mathcal O_S$; existence of a good model after enlarging $S$.
- *The de Rham bundle* $\mathcal H = \pi_* H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(X/Y')$ over $\mathcal E = \pi_*\mathcal O_{Y'}$, with
  Hodge sub-bundle, $\mathcal E$-bilinear polarization for which $F^1$ is Lagrangian, and Gauss–Manin connection.
- *Residue disks* $\Omega_v(y_0)\cong(p\mathcal O_v)^m$ for $v \notin S$ with $K_v/\mathbb Q_p$ unramified and $p>2$.
- *Formal horizontal sections* with $\alpha!\,\Phi_\alpha$ integral, their $v$-adic convergence on the residue
  disk (Legendre's bound) and their complex convergence near $0$ (majorants).
- *Gauss–Manin transport* $T_v(y)$ and $T_{\mathbb C}(y)$ (LV (3.7), (3.8)), compatible with the
  $\mathcal E$-structure (LV (6.3)–(6.6)) and the polarization; $T_{\mathbb C}$ is Betti parallel transport.
- *Crystalline Frobenius on the fibres* $\varphi_y$ and $T_v(y)\circ\varphi_{y_0}=\varphi_y\circ T_v(y)$ (LV (3.9)).

**Inputs.** Abelian schemes, polarizations and degree-one de Rham realizations (`AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli`
A1, A2, A4), complex uniformization and the Betti local system (A5), relative Gauss–Manin compatibility of the
de Rham–Betti comparison (`ComplexComparisonPartII` C5), crystals, the Berthelot–Ogus comparison, crystalline
Frobenius and the relative Gauss–Manin interface (`CrystallineCohomology` CR.1, CR.2, CR.3, CR.7), spreading out and
completed local rings (`SchemeAndStackFoundations` SF.0), unramified local fields (`LocalFieldsRamification` Layer 2).

**Acceptance.** The Legendre family over $\mathbb Z[1/2][t,1/(t(1-t))]$ is a good model; for the constant family
the transport is the identity; for $p=3$ the series $\exp(z)$ converges on $3\mathbb Z_3$, while for $p=2$ it
does not converge on $2\mathbb Z_2$.

stages.title: Lagrangian period varieties and the complex and p-adic period maps
stages.description:
Period maps on residue disks and the transfer of Zariski density from the complex to the $p$-adic side
(LV §§3.2–3.4), specialized to the degree-one cohomology of abelian-by-finite families.

**Targets.**
- *Lagrangian linear algebra*: adapted symplectic bases, transitivity of $\mathrm{Sp}$ on Lagrangians, graphs of
  symmetric maps, Arnold's transversality lemma; the *Lagrangian Grassmannian* $\mathrm{LGr}(V,\omega)$ as a
  closed subscheme of Mathlib's Grassmannian, smooth, projective, geometrically irreducible of dimension
  $d(d+1)/2$.
- *Lagrangian period variety* $\mathrm{LGr}_E(V,\omega)$ for a finite étale $K$-algebra $E$ (LV's
  $\mathrm{Res}^E_K\mathrm{LGr}$), its splitting over a field splitting $E$, dimension $[E:K]\,d(d+1)/2$,
  product decomposition and factor projections; the Grassmannian of $E$-stable subspaces.
- *Algebraic monodromy group* $\Gamma$ (LV (3.5)) and *full monodromy* (LV (5.1)).
- *Period maps*: $\Phi_v(y)=T_v(y)^{-1}(F^1\mathcal H_y)$ on $\Omega_v(y_0)$, compatible with Frobenius;
  $\Phi_{\mathbb C}$ and its equivariant continuation to the universal cover; both given in Plücker coordinates
  by one tuple of power series over $K$, restricted over $\mathcal O_v$ after $z = px$.
- *LV Lemma 3.1* ($\Gamma\cdot h_0\subseteq\overline{\Phi_{\mathbb C}(U)}$), *LV Lemma 3.2* (common $K$-form of
  the $v$-adic and complex Zariski closures of a power-series map), *LV Lemma 3.3* and density of
  $\Phi_v(\Omega_v)$ under full monodromy.
- *Strassmann's theorem* and *finiteness of preimages*: on a curve, $\Phi_v$ meets a closed subset not containing
  its image, or of dimension smaller than its Zariski closure, in finitely many points; the same for factor
  projections.

**Inputs.** Grassmannian schemes, Plücker embeddings and closed conditions (`AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry`
R09.1), dimension theory (`SchemeAndStackFoundations` SF.0), orbit maps and Zariski closures (`ReductiveGroups`
Layer 3), the Betti local system and Gauss–Manin compatibility (`AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli` A5,
`ComplexComparisonPartII` C5), algebraic versus analytic local rings (C0), connectedness of $Y(\mathbb C)$ (C4),
universal covers (`UniversalCovers` Stage 2).

**Acceptance.** For $E=K$, $d=1$ the period variety is $\mathbb P^1$ and $\mathrm{LGr}$ of a $4$-dimensional space
is a quadric threefold; Strassmann's bound for $1+pX+X^2+pX^5$ over $\mathbb Q_p$ is $2$, attained for $p=5$; the
Legendre period map is nonconstant on every residue disk; a constant family has zero-dimensional closure.

stages.title: Crystalline comparison on residue disks and the finiteness criterion
stages.description:
The bridge from Galois representations to the period map (LV §3.5, and the indexing of §6).

**Targets.**
- *Fibre representations*: for $y\in Y(K)$ in the residue disk, $y'$ over $y$ and $w\mid v$,
  $\rho_{y',w}=H^1_{\mathrm{et}}(X_{y'},\mathbb Q_p)|_{G_{K(y')_w}}$ is crystalline with
  $D_{\mathrm{cris}}(\rho_{y',w})\cong(H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(X_{y'}/K(y')_w),\varphi,F^1)$.
- *Transport* (LV (6.6)–(6.7)): this filtered $\varphi$-module is, along the transported field isomorphism, the
  factor $(V_0,\varphi_0,\mathrm{pr}_0\Phi_v(y))$ of the base fibre.
- *Orbit lemma*: filtrations with isomorphic filtered $\varphi$-modules form one $Z(\varphi)^\times$-orbit, inside
  the $K_v$-points of the unit group of $Z(\varphi^{f_v})$, whose orbit closures have dimension
  $\le\dim_{K_v}Z(\varphi^{f_v})\le(\dim V)^2$.
- *Finiteness criterion*: on a curve, if $\dim_{K_v}Z(\varphi_0^{f_v})$ is smaller than the dimension of the
  closure of $\mathrm{pr}_0\Phi_v(\Omega_v)$, the points of the disk whose local pairs
  $(K(y')_w,\rho_{y',w})$ lie in finitely many classes are finitely many; under full monodromy this holds when
  $[K(y')_w:K_v]\ge8$.
- *LV Proposition 3.4* for polarized abelian schemes over a curve: under (3.13), finitely many $y\in Y(\mathcal O)$
  in a residue disk have $\rho_y$ semisimple.

**Inputs.** Filtered $\varphi$-modules and $D_{\mathrm{cris}}$ (`PadicHodgeTheory` R06.2), the crystalline
comparison (`CohomologyComparisons` CP.2 node) and its identification with Berthelot–Ogus and the Hodge filtration
(R06.5), crystallinity for good reduction (R06.6), the Berthelot–Ogus isomorphism (`CrystallineCohomology` CR.2),
base change of étale cohomology (`SchemeAndStackFoundations` SF.2), dimension theory (SF.0), orbit closures
(`ReductiveGroups` Layer 3), unramified local fields (`LocalFieldsRamification` Layer 2), Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich
(`NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties` R11.5).

**Acceptance.** Over $K_v=\mathbb Q_p$ a good-reduction elliptic curve has $\dim Z(\varphi)=2$ (ordinary or
supersingular); over $K_v=\mathbb Q_{p^2}$ a supersingular curve over $\mathbb Q_p$ with $a_p=0$ has
$\varphi^2=-p$ and $\dim Z(\varphi^2)=4$, an ordinary one $2$; (3.13) fails for the Legendre family
($2>1$, LV §1.3).

stages.title: Surfaces, mapping class groups and families of branched covers
stages.description:
Surface topology in the form used by LV §8 and by the Legendre monodromy of §4 (Farb–Margalit, Chapters 1–6).
No atlas roadmap owns this material; the packet's restructure proposal moves it to a new roadmap.

**Targets.**
- *Surfaces* with boundary and punctures, their type $(g,b,n)$, simple closed curves and the intersection form;
  the *classification of compact surfaces*.
- *Mapping class groups* $\mathrm{Mod}(S)$ and $\mathrm{Mod}(S^*)$ with their actions on homology, curves and
  finite coverings; the *change of coordinates* principle for nonseparating curves, pairs meeting once and
  geometric symplectic bases.
- *Dehn twists* and their action on homology, $\Psi(T_b^k)(x)=x+k\,\hat\imath(x,b)[b]$, multitwists;
  primitive classes are represented by simple closed curves (Farb–Margalit Proposition 6.2); surjectivity of
  $\mathrm{Mod}(S_g)\to\mathrm{Sp}(2g,\mathbb Z)$ (Theorem 6.4); capping (Proposition 3.19).
- *Point pushing*: the Birman exact sequence and $\mathrm{Push}(\alpha)=T_aT_b^{-1}$ (Theorem 4.6, Fact 4.7).
- *Configuration fibration* $F(S)\to S$, exactness of $\pi_1(S\smallsetminus y)\to\pi_1(F(S))\to\pi_1(S)\to1$,
  preservation of the peripheral class, and the free presentation of a punctured closed surface group.
- *Lifting twists to coverings* ($T_e^{n_e}$ lifts to $\prod T_{e_i}^{n_e/d_i}$) and the *monodromy of families of
  branched covers* over configuration spaces as lifted point-pushing maps.

**Inputs.** Van Kampen (`AlgebraicTopology` Stage 1), singular homology and local systems (Stage 2), CW structures
(Stage 4), duality and intersection pairings (Stage 6), fibration sequences (Stage 8), covering spaces
(`UniversalCovers` Stage 2), cutting, gluing, collars and isotopy extension (`GeometricTopology` Layer 1).

**Acceptance.** $\mathrm{Mod}$ of an annulus is $\mathbb Z$; on the torus $T_b$ acts by an elementary matrix;
$(2,0)\in H_1(T^2)$ is not represented by a simple closed curve while $(2,3)$ is; for the thrice-punctured sphere
a push around one puncture is a single twist.

stages.title: The S-unit theorem
stages.description:
The first worked instance of the method (LV §4, Theorem 4.1).

**Targets.**
- *Reductions*: enlarging $K$ and $S$ ($\mu_8\subseteq K$, places above $2$ in $S$), $U\subseteq\bigcup_j U_1^{2^j}$
  with $U_1$ the non-square solutions; the Kummer fields $K(t^{1/m})$ (cyclic of degree $m$, unramified outside
  $S$, finitely many); an auxiliary place $v$ whose Frobenius generates $\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$, so $v$ is inert.
- *The Legendre family* as an elliptic scheme over $\mathbb P^1_{\mathcal O}\smallsetminus\{0,1,\infty\}$ and its
  cyclic variant $X\to\mathbb P^1\smallsetminus\{0,\mu_m,\infty\}\xrightarrow{u\mapsto u^m}\mathbb P^1\smallsetminus\{0,1,\infty\}$
  as an abelian-by-finite family with good model.
- *Legendre monodromy*: the loops around $0$ and $1$ act by $\pm T_a^2$ and $\pm T_b^2$ with
  $\hat\imath(a,b)=\pm1$ (derived from point pushing and twist lifting), so the family has full monodromy.
- *LV Lemma 4.3* (full monodromy of the variant family) via a factorwise-unipotent criterion for closed
  subgroups of $\prod\mathrm{SL}_2$.
- *LV Lemma 4.4* (generic simplicity of $V_p(E_z)$, via Lemma 2.10, weak admissibility and the finiteness of
  preimages), *LV Lemma 4.2* (finiteness in a residue disk) and *LV Theorem 4.1*.

**Inputs.** Kummer theory and standard étale algebras (Mathlib), Hermite–Minkowski
(`FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems` R28.1 node), Chebotarev (Layer 10), unramified local extensions
(`LocalFieldsRamification` Layer 2), elliptic schemes, polarizations, de Rham realizations and complex
uniformization (`AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli` A1, A2, A4, A5), Gauss–Manin compatibility
(`ComplexComparisonPartII` C5), connectedness (C4), closed normal subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_2$ and Zariski closures
(`ReductiveGroups` Layers 3, 6), covering spaces (`UniversalCovers` Stage 2), weak admissibility (`PadicHodgeTheory`
R06.2), purity of subrepresentations (`WeightsInEtaleCohomology` R34.1), LV.0–LV.5.

**Acceptance.** $K=\mathbb Q$, $S=\{2,\infty\}$ gives $U=\{-1,2,1/2\}$, all with $j=1728$; for
$K=\mathbb Q(\zeta_8)$, $m=8$ and the centralizer bound $4<8$; in a basis with $\hat\imath(a,b)=1$ the monodromy
contains $\begin{psmallmatrix}1&-2\\0&1\end{psmallmatrix}$ and $\begin{psmallmatrix}1&0\\2&1\end{psmallmatrix}$;
for $p=3$ and $z\equiv2\bmod3$ the curve is supersingular and never reducible.

stages.title: Rational points on the base of an abelian-by-finite family
stages.description:
The refined criterion for curves (LV §5 Definition 5.2, Proposition 5.3, §6).

**Targets.**
- *$\mathrm{size}_v$* (LV Definition 5.2), its independence of choices and the monotonicity (5.3); Frobenius
  orbits on geometric points as places above $v$, of sizes $[E_w:K_v]$.
- *LV Lemma 6.4* (general position of $r\ge5$ Lagrangians) and *LV Lemma 6.3* (for a cyclic extension of degree
  $r\ge5$ and a semilinear Frobenius similitude, the Lagrangians meeting a nonzero proper Frobenius-stable subspace
  in half its dimension lie in a proper closed subset).
- *The Sublemma*, *LV Lemma 6.1* (generic simplicity along the family, taking the union over all base pairs of
  local degree $\ge8$) and *LV Lemma 6.2* (Galois representations vary).
- *LV Proposition 5.3*: for a smooth projective geometrically connected curve $Y$, an abelian-by-finite family with
  full monodromy and a good model with $\mathcal Y$ proper, and a friendly place $v\notin S$ with odd residue
  characteristic lying below no place of $S$, $\{y\in Y(K):\mathrm{size}_v(\pi^{-1}(y))<1/(d+1)\}$ is finite.

**Inputs.** Unramified local fields and decomposition groups (`LocalFieldsRamification` Layer 2), projectivity of
Grassmannians and rank conditions (`AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry` R09.1), dimension theory and images under
finite maps (`SchemeAndStackFoundations` SF.0), $D_{\mathrm{cris}}$ of subrepresentations (`PadicHodgeTheory` R06.2),
purity (`WeightsInEtaleCohomology` R34.1), connectedness (`ComplexComparisonPartII` C4), Hermite–Minkowski
(`FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems` R28.1 node), Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich (R11.5), LV.0–LV.4.

**Acceptance.** For $d=1$ the bad locus of Lemma 6.4 is the small diagonal; the four Lagrangians of LV p. 34 for
$d=2$; a single Frobenius $k$-cycle has $\mathrm{size}_v$ equal to $1$ if $k<8$ and $0$ otherwise; for $\pi=\mathrm{id}$
the proposition is empty.

stages.title: Hurwitz spaces of singly ramified covers and the Kodaira–Parshin family
stages.description:
The auxiliary family (LV §7) and the fibre map (5.5).

**Targets.**
- *Topology of $Y(\mathbb C)$*: a connected closed surface of genus $g$ with the free presentation of
  $\pi_1(Y(\mathbb C)\smallsetminus y)$.
- *Group theory* (LV Lemma 7.4): $S(\Gamma,c,G)$ with commuting $\Gamma$- and $G$-actions for centre-free $G$, and
  the unique extension of the action to overgroups normalizing $\Gamma$ and preserving $c$ (only middle exactness of
  the fundamental-group sequence is needed).
- *Complex Hurwitz space* (LV §7.3) as a covering of the configuration space, algebraized by Riemann existence and
  normalization, with its local form along the branch divisor.
- *Descent* (LV Lemma 7.4) and *LV Proposition 7.1*: $\pi:Y'\to Y$ finite étale with
  $\pi^{-1}(y)$ the conjugacy classes of surjections $\pi_1^{\mathrm{geom}}(Y\smallsetminus y)\to G$ nontrivial at
  $y$, $G_K$-equivariantly for $y\in Y(K)$ (defined through the outer action), and the universal relative curve.
- *Reduced Pryms*: the idempotents $e, e', e''$ of $\mathbb Q[\mathrm{Aff}(q)]$; $X=(\ker e'')^\circ$ in
  $\mathrm{Pic}^0$; its rational homology is the primitive homology of the degree-$q$ cover, of dimension
  $(2g-1)(q-1)$.
- *The Kodaira–Parshin family* (LV Definitions 7.2, 7.3) of relative dimension $d_q=(g-\tfrac12)(q-1)$ with a good
  model, and the *fibre map* (5.5) to $H^1_{\mathrm{et}}(Y_{\bar K},\mathbb Z/(q-1))$ with image the generating
  tuples and fibres of size $q^{2g-2}$.

**Inputs.** Riemann existence and invariance of étale fundamental groups (`InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups`
IG.3), Galois categories and the arithmetic sequence (IG.0, IG.1), analytification and GAGA (`ComplexComparisonPartII`
C0, C2, C4), de Rham–Betti comparison (C5), genus of curves (`AlgebraicCurves` Layer 3, `SchemeAndStackFoundations`
SF.3), normalization (SF.0), relative Picard schemes (`JacobianChallenge` Layer D,
`AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry` A0-extension), abelian subschemes, polarizations and complex uniformization
(`AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli` A1, A2, A5), transfer and duality (`AlgebraicTopology` Stages 5, 6), covering
spaces (`UniversalCovers` Stage 2), Poincaré duality for curves with torsion coefficients
(`EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves` EDC.2), LV.0, LV.2, LV.5.

**Acceptance.** For $G=\mathrm{Aff}(3)\cong S_3$ and $g=2$ there are $810$ surjections nontrivial around the branch
point, so each fibre of $Y'\to Y$ has $135$ points, the degree-$3$ covers have genus $5$, $d_3=3$, and the fibre
map has image of size $15$ with fibres of size $9$.

stages.title: Aff(q)-covers of surfaces: primitive homology, lifted monodromy and normal form
stages.description:
The topological set-up of LV §§8.2–8.4 and Lemma 8.11.

**Targets.**
- *$\mathrm{Aff}(q)$-covers* and *singly ramified* $\mathrm{Aff}(q)$-covers of $(Y,y)$: isomorphism classes as
  $\mathrm{Aff}(q)$-conjugacy classes of monodromy, genus $gq-(q-1)/2$, finitely many.
- *Primitive homology* $H_1^{\mathrm{Pr}}(Z,Y)=\ker\pi_*=(\pi^*H_1(Y))^\perp$ with its symplectic form.
- *Lifted monodromy* (LV (8.2)–(8.5)): unique lifts of stabilizing mapping classes, $\mathrm{Mon}_Z$, the finite-index
  normal subgroups $\mathrm{Mod}(Y\smallsetminus y)'$ and $\pi_1(Y,y)'$; lifts of point pushes are trivial on
  $\pi^*H_1(Y)$.
- *LV Lemma 8.2* and *Lemma 8.3* for nonseparating curves (independence of preimage classes; the rank $k-1$ of a
  lifted twist detects the cycle type); *liftable curves*, the transvection $T_{\tilde e}^q$ and (8.6).
- *LV Lemma 8.4* (surjectivity onto $\mathrm{Sp}(V,b)$ for two boundary circles, with its consequences for arcs and
  for classes $v+kb$), *LV Proposition 8.5* (normal form $Y=S_{g-1}\#T$) and *LV Lemma 8.11* (the curves
  $\gamma_j=T_d^k(\beta_1)$ on $T^\circ$).

**Inputs.** Covering spaces (`UniversalCovers` Stage 2), van Kampen (`AlgebraicTopology` Stage 1), cellular homology
of graphs (Stage 4), transfer (Stage 5), Poincaré–Lefschetz duality (Stage 6), cutting and gluing
(`GeometricTopology` Layer 1), Schreier's lemma (Mathlib), LV.0, LV.5.

**Acceptance.** For $q=3$, $g=2$ there are $135$ covers of genus $5$ with $6$-dimensional primitive homology; for
$q=5$ the cycle types of the identity, a $5$-cycle and elements with linear part of order $2$ or $4$ have
$k=5,1,3,2$; for a torus with two holes $\mathrm{Sp}(V,b)\cong\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)\ltimes\mathbb Z^2$.

stages.title: The monodromy theorem for Kodaira–Parshin families
stages.description:
Big monodromy (LV §§8.2.3, 8.5, 8.6).

**Targets.**
- *LV Lemma 8.6* (proved here): a power of the push along a finger-moved nonseparating curve acts on each
  $H_1^{\mathrm{Pr}}(Z_i,Y)$ as a nontrivial unipotent.
- *LV Lemma 8.8* (distinct covers are distinguished by the cycle type along a nonseparating simple closed curve;
  in the last case the curve is constructed as a twist $T_d^m(x)$).
- *LV Lemma 8.10* (a connected spanning system of liftable curves), *Lemma 8.9* (density on one factor),
  *Lemma 8.7* (density on the product, via LV Lemma 2.12), closed normal subgroups of products of symplectic groups,
  and *LV Theorem 8.1* (Zariski density of $\mathrm{Mon}\circ\mathrm{Push}$ on $\pi_1(Y,y)'$).
- *Full monodromy of the Kodaira–Parshin family* (LV §8.2.3, property (i) before Theorem 5.4), through the
  configuration-family comparison and the homology of reduced Pryms.

**Inputs.** Zariski closures and closed normal subgroups of $\mathrm{Sp}$ (`ReductiveGroups` Layers 3, 6), van Kampen
and Mayer–Vietoris (`AlgebraicTopology` Stages 1, 3), the Betti local system of abelian schemes and Gauss–Manin
compatibility (`AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli` A5, `ComplexComparisonPartII` C5), LV.0, LV.3, LV.5, LV.8, LV.9.

**Acceptance.** For $g=2$, $q=3$ the closure is a product of $135$ copies of $\mathrm{Sp}_6$; the unipotent of
Lemma 8.6 has $u-1$ of rank $2$ there; the subgroup $\{\pm1\}^N$ shows that non-centrality is needed.

stages.title: Faltings's theorem after Lawrence and Venkatesh
stages.description:
The assembly (LV Theorem 5.4).

**Targets.**
- *Choice of $q$*: arbitrarily large primes $q$ with $4\nmid q-1$, no odd prime below $8[K:\mathbb Q]$ or dividing
  $\mathrm{disc}(K)$ dividing $q-1$, so that $\mathrm{Gal}(K'(\zeta_{q-1})/\mathbb Q)\cong
  \mathrm{Gal}(K'/\mathbb Q)\times(\mathbb Z/(q-1))^\times$, and $8\cdot2^{g+1}/(q-1)^g<1/((g-\tfrac12)(q-1)+1)$.
- *Choice of $v$*: a friendly place with odd residue characteristic outside a given finite set, $(q_v,q-1)=1$ and
  $q_v$ of order $\ge8$ modulo every odd prime divisor of $q-1$ (Chebotarev in $K'(\zeta_{m'})/\mathbb Q$).
- *The Weil pairing* on $M=H^1_{\mathrm{et}}(Y_{\bar K},\mathbb Z/(q-1))$ with
  $\langle Tm_1,Tm_2\rangle=q_v^{-1}\langle m_1,m_2\rangle$.
- *Small-orbit count*: $|\ker(T^i-1)|\le2^g(q-1)^g$ for $1\le i\le7$.
- *Size bound* (LV (5.4)) and *Faltings's theorem*: a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus
  $g\ge2$ over a number field has finitely many rational points.

**Inputs.** Dirichlet's theorem, discriminants and Minkowski's theorem (Mathlib), the cyclotomic compositum and its
Frobenius (Tau Ceti), Chebotarev (Layer 10), unramified primes of Galois closures (`LocalFieldsRamification`
Layer 2), Poincaré duality for curves with torsion coefficients (`EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves` EDC.2), étale
$H^1$ and outer Galois actions (`InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups` IG.1), connectedness
(`ComplexComparisonPartII` C4), LV.0, LV.1, LV.2, LV.7, LV.8, LV.10.

**Acceptance.** For $K=\mathbb Q$ and $g=2$, $q=107$ is admissible ($106=2\cdot53$, $64/106^2<1/160$), $d_q=159$,
and $v$ can be any odd prime $p\equiv2\bmod53$, e.g. $p=373$; the final statement is the one stated by
`HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions` RP.4.
